item.text: {"verdicts":[{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E001","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E002","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E003","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"Support for higher military spending increased by 26 percentage points, opposition to recognizing Russia’s annexation of Crimea increased by 25 points, support for a more confrontational Russia policy increased by 16 points, and support for good relations with Putin declined by 23 points.","notes":["The excerpt supports the quantities and directions but does not specify the German Longitudinal Election Study panel or the December 2021-to-May 2022 dates."]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E004","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E005","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E006","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E007","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E008","status":"accepted","corrected_fact_summary":null,"notes":[]},{"evidence_id":"BATCH-0034-R08-E009","status":"corrected","corrected_fact_summary":"The authors report that changes in opinion were concentrated on war-related policy issues, while core postures and attitudes toward unrelated issues and actors remained stable; they reject the thesis of a turning point in German public opinion.","notes":["The excerpt supports rejection of the turning-point thesis and the reported stability, but the phrase “insufficient evidence” is narrower than the excerpt’s stated conclusion."]}]}
